clue.text: One in conspiracy to control ship

indicators.note: the word for the conspiracy holds the numeral for one inside it

parts.note: a conspiracy is a plot

explanation.surface: Someone in a mutinous plot aims to seize command of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or navigate a vessel.

clue.text: Dispensary is pretty lively taking in injury

indicators.note: the word for pretty lively takes in the injury word, so one surrounds the other

parts.note: pacy means quick, lively
injury is harm

explanation.surface: A busy chemist's shop is also treating the wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a shop or hospital department dispensing medicines.

clue.text: Sonia and, after fifty, involved in affair

indicators.note: the jumbled names come after the Roman fifty in the answer

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Sonia and the speaker, past fifty, are tangled in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost the 'I' that the wordplay needs. 'involved' mixes SONIA plus I into IAISON, placed after L.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret love relationship.

clue.text: Time to have DIY repair made neat

indicators.note: repair here means rework, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing a home repair job takes time but leaves things looking smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges DIY into IDY after T; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and neat both describe something orderly.

clue.text: Fare from France, dead slow?

parts.note: a French dish that is also a creature famous for moving at a crawl

explanation.surface: A traveller complains about French transport being very slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price and 'dead slow' a train, but it is food: a snail, served in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are cooked as a French delicacy and are proverbially slow-moving.

clue.text: Crackdown boss who welcomes stoppages at work?

definitions.text: Crackdown boss who welcomes stoppages at work?

parts.words: Crackdown boss who welcomes stoppages at work?
parts.note: a railway boss whose business is trains stopping, including fast 'down' trains

explanation.surface: A boss in charge of a crackdown oddly enjoys strikes at the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoppages' suggests strikes, but here trains are stopping at a platform; a crack 'down' train is a fast one heading away from London.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a railway stop is happy when trains halt there.

clue.text: Chief feature of perpendicular church?

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: What is the main element of a church in the Perpendicular Gothic style?
explanation.walkthrough: An arch is also a genuine feature of a Perpendicular church, so the surface describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means principal, as in archenemy.

clue.text: Postage changes for policemen feared

indicators.note: changes tells us the word postage is rearranged

explanation.surface: Higher postal charges are feared by officers of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's dreaded secret police force.

clue.text: House-doctor out, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The house doctor is out, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DR plus OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were an English royal dynasty, and a royal family line is called a house.

clue.text: River Test is extremely tedious for shipbuilders and the like

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a test is a trial

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Fishing the River Test, a Hampshire chalk stream, proves very boring for some.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's '5' is an OCR misreading of 'is'. 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'tedious', T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipbuilders are examples of people who run large manufacturing businesses.

clue.text: Light rubber producing a powerful spirit

definitions.text: Light rubber producing a powerful spirit

parts.words: Light rubber producing a powerful spirit
parts.note: the folk-tale youth who rubbed a magic lamp and summoned a genie

explanation.surface: Polishing something brings out a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is the lamp and 'spirit' the genie, not a weak eraser or alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero rubs a lamp and a genie appears.

clue.text: Copper in case, perhaps, deserted the one charged

indicators.note: the copper symbol goes inside the reworked case
perhaps hints at a variant arrangement of the letters of case

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
D is a standard abbreviation for deserted, as in naval records

explanation.surface: A policeman, in a case left abandoned, is the person facing charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CASE into ACSE; CU goes inside it after AC, and D ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant in a trial is the person against whom charges are laid.

clue.text: New wine upsets tums

indicators.note: upsets means knocks into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Young wine gives people stomach troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Must is grape juice that has not yet finished fermenting.

clue.text: Nobody's child? What a bloomer:!

explanation.surface: An unwanted orphan turns out to be a spectacular mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Diary of a Nobody, a classic English comic novel, Charles Pooter's son is called Lupin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupin is the son of the diarist Pooter, the 'Nobody'; and a lupin is a tall garden flower, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Reasonable trade-show

explanation.surface: A sensible exhibition for merchants.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or moderate; a fair is also a commercial exhibition.

clue.text: Sort of being kind?

parts.note: the word that goes with being and with kind to make two familiar phrases about people

explanation.surface: Is this a form of kindness?
explanation.walkthrough: The word completes both 'human being' and 'humankind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a human being, and people together are humankind.

clue.text: Mind the bad weather at Beachy Head

indicators.note: head of a word is its first letter, here of Beachy

parts.note: rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Watch out for rain on the clifftops at Beachy Head, the Sussex headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a high chalk headland on England's south coast. 'Head' takes its B, which comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of thought, the seat of the intellect.

clue.text: Doctor not there?--So ring locum, not get excited

indicators.note: letters that get excited are stirred up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: With the doctor away, a patient is told to phone the stand-in calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors see patients in their surgery, so if one isn't there, that is where to look.

clue.text: Wiper of L-car seen to be loose

indicators.note: letters let loose fall into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The windscreen wiper on a learner driver's car has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-car is a car carrying a learner's L plate in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is something used to wipe surfaces clean.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument is at Hebridean, left behind. What sort of ability is needed to get it?

definitions.text: What sort of ability is needed to get it?

indicators.note: behind places the abbreviation for left at the end

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An organ stands on a Scottish island, abandoned; what skill does it take to fetch it?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second sentence: getting a large organ moved needs planning skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging such a move calls for planning and administrative skill.

clue.text: Spring-lock?

parts.note: a lock of hair that coils like a spring, not a security device

explanation.surface: A kind of door lock that snaps shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A curled tress of hair hangs in a corkscrew shape.

clue.text: Working at it, there is generally room for improvement

definitions.text: Working at it, there is generally room for improvement

parts.words: Working at it, there is generally room for improvement
parts.note: a profession practised in hospitals, where wards are rooms in which patients get better

explanation.surface: Anyone trying hard always has scope to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room for improvement' is a stock phrase for imperfect work, but here it is a ward where the sick recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for patients takes place in rooms where they recover their health.

clue.text: Old Spanish wine some guys keep down

explanation.surface: Some men hold down a vintage Spanish red.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent was a deep red wine from Spain; a canvas shelter is pegged down by guy ropes.

clue.text: Wild brute of the underground system

definitions.note: the definition names something belonging to a plant's underground parts

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: A savage creature roams the London Tube network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground system' suggests the London Underground, but it is the root system of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a swollen stem growing below the soil, part of a plant's buried structure.

clue.text: Blind open — water coming in-novel kind of house!

indicators.note: open means the opening letter of the word blind

parts.note: a leak lets water in

explanation.surface: With the blind up, rain gets in; what a strange house!
explanation.walkthrough: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens title names a house with that adjective, so the word describes a house in fiction.

clue.text: Bangor-Caernarvon part of Wales, we hear

definitions.note: Wales spoken sounds like whales, the sea creatures

indicators.note: part of says the letters form a portion of the names given

explanation.surface: Bangor and Caernarvon are towns in North Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wales, we hear' is the definition, sounding like 'whales'; the answer is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is one of the large marine mammals of the whale family.

clue.text: See the gathering!

explanation.surface: Look at the crowd!
explanation.walkthrough: A gathering is an old word for an abscess or boil coming to a head.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the skin is called a gathering when it fills with pus.

clue.text: Detect Green's position at table?

explanation.surface: Notice where the green ball sits on the snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a British cue game, each coloured ball such as the green has a marked spot on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice; the green ball's marked place on the baize has the same name.

clue.text: Flute fixed them, the loud roars

explanation.surface: A flute was repaired with loud roaring noises.
explanation.walkthrough: Flute is Bellows-Mender in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he mends them.

clue.text: Pit seem to be prepared for dead men?

explanation.definitionFit: Finished bottles are called dead men or dead soldiers.

clue.text: Girl belittled is without mercy

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name
something belittled is made smaller, made less

explanation.surface: Putting a girl down is a cruel thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means pitiless, showing no compassion.

clue.text: Blake's night-burner?

parts.note: William Blake's poem has a big cat burning bright in the forests of the night

explanation.surface: Something a poet lit at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake spelt the big cat with a Y in his poem's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem describes the striped beast burning bright in the night.
